<!-- docs-drift-check -->
### 📓 Docs Drift Check
Nothing in this diff resolved to a documentable surface (no symbol, route or SDK anchor derived from **0** changed package(s)), so **this run has no opinion** about the docs.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **0** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 04273b9b2cdcadcc90c3fb44861625bddc91816e` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

CI on `597471c344`: the `Lint & Repo Gates` lane was red on two gates, everything else green (the four `* UI` jobs skipped as designed, Test Core still running at the time).

| gate | why red | fix in `7ca50a8a7b` |
|---|---|---|
| `Dispatcher error-code vocabulary guard` (`check:dispatcher-error-vocabulary`) | refuses any `pnpm-workspace.yaml` glob that expands to no member (#16649); the four `ui` globs match nothing until the import | `WORKSPACE_GLOBS_AWAITING_IMPORT` excuses exactly those four, only while `ui/package.json` is absent (`awaitingImportGlobs`); opt-in at the call site, self-test pins the key set, holds every key against the live workspace, and drives both marker states on a scratch root |
| `Duration-shaped spec keys carry their unit in the key name` (`packages/spec` `check:duration-unit-keys`) | mirrors the workspace roots as `ROOT_DIR_WATCH_HINTS` literals and holds them against the live file in both directions | the four roots declared as `ui/src/**`, `ui/packages/*/src/**`, `ui/apps/*/src/**`, `ui/examples/*/src/**` |

Neither gate is in the `dispatch-gates --commands` derivation for this PR's paths, which is why the local sweep did not catch them. Reproduced on the PR merge commit (`refs/pull/25710/merge`), both exit 1 before and 0 after; the 80 gate commands the derivation names for the two edited files: 76 exit 0, 4 exit 3 NOT MEASURED (`check:dts-closure`, `check:dual-build-cjs-loads`, `check:lean-entry-closure`, `check:sourcemap-no-sources-content` need a built `dist/`; they do not read either edited file and were green in CI on the previous head). eslint on both files exit 0.

The approval already on record is unaffected by the push (unpinned since 2026-09-04); auto-merge stays armed. Changed lines are now 1,019 (+1,019 / −33 → 1,052 total), still under the human-merge line.
